speaker: VANESSA
line: Of what?

speaker: FISK
line: The way you'd look at me if you knew.

speaker: VANESSA
line: Tell me.

speaker: BILL
line: Shut up! No, please! Shut up! I don't wanna hear it! I lost because of you!

speaker: MARLENE
line: No!

speaker: BILL
line: Because of this family.

speaker: MARLENE
line: No!

speaker: BILL
line: They see it! They see you and that little bastard and they laugh! And you don't believe in me!

speaker: MARLENE
line: I do.

speaker: BILL
line: And you see what happens?

speaker: MARLENE
line: No!

speaker: BILL
line: You see what happens?

speaker: MARLENE
line: No! Oh, God, no!

speaker: BILL
line: You don't believe in me! Shut up! Stop it! What are you gonna do with that, fatty? Huh? Huh? That's what I thought. You believe this kid? He gets that shit from you.

speaker: MARLENE
line: Oh, God.

speaker: MARLENE
line: Keep kicking him! Keep kicking him! Keep kicking him! Keep kicking him! Wilson—

speaker: YOUNG WILSON
line: It's okay.

speaker: MARLENE
line: Mommy.

speaker: YOUNG WILSON
line: It's all right. It's all right, baby. It's all right.

speaker: MARLENE
line: It's all right. It's okay. It's okay, baby. It's okay. Okay. Get the saw.

speaker: FISK
line: We carried him in bags down to the river. One every night, for the next week. Everyone in town knew that he owed money to Rigoletto. So, I guess they thought that he'd left town to avoid him. My mother, she sent me to live with relatives on the farm that I told you about.

speaker: VANESSA
line: It wasn't your fault. You were protecting your mother.

speaker: FISK
line: I didn't do it for her. I did it for me. That's why I still wear these. To remind myself that I'm not cruel for the sake of cruelty! That I'm not my father! That I'm not a monster! Am I?

speaker: VANESSA
line: No, Wilson. You aren't.

speaker: FISK
line: But soon it won't matter. There are people out there that want to expose me. They don't understand what I'm trying to do for this city. They want to drag my name through the streets! They want to destroy everything that I'm trying to accomplish.

speaker: VANESSA
line: And are you going to let them?

speaker: FISK
line: No.

speaker: BEN
line: It was a total bust. No, I... Ellison. Ellison, no— He's a crazy old man in a tinfoil hat. And why are we chasing a story like this anyway? What? Shit. Look, can I call you back? I'm drowning out here. Yes, yes, okay. Fine.

speaker: MATT
line: We need to talk. Do you know who I am?

speaker: BEN
line: The Devil of Hell's Kitchen.

speaker: MATT
line: Do you believe that? What they're saying about me?

speaker: BEN
line: You've been in an awful lot of wrong places at the wrong time lately. But I've heard the other stories. About the man in the mask, helping people. Sounds like maybe there's more than one side to you.

speaker: MATT
line: I didn't blow the hell out of the Russians. And I didn't shoot those cops.

speaker: BEN
line: So, what?

speaker: MATT
line: You want me to write your side of this?

speaker: BEN
line: No, I want you to expose the man responsible. The man who's tearing this city apart, piece by piece.

speaker: BEN
line: You got a name?

speaker: MATT
line: Wilson Fisk.

speaker: BEN
line: Never heard of him.

speaker: MATT
line: Because he doesn't want you to. That's what makes him dangerous. Living in the shadows, no one knowing who he is.

speaker: BEN
line: Said the man in the mask.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm trying to protect this city.

speaker: BEN
line: Maybe. But right now they hate you. And have no idea who this Fisk guy is.

speaker: MATT
line: You can change that.

speaker: BEN
line: So could 100 other reporters. Why me?

speaker: MATT
line: There are good people who trust you, Ben. I have faith in their judgment.

speaker: BEN
line: Union Allied. Guessing that was you who dumped that guy on the doorsteps of the Bulletin?

speaker: MATT
line: I think he's connected to Fisk.

speaker: BEN
line: That woman you saved that night? She's a good kid. Still believes you're a hero, despite what everybody's saying. People like her are why I do this. If I do the smart thing and say no?

speaker: MATT
line: Then I'll have to stop him some other way.

speaker: BEN
line: That has a ring of finality to it.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm not a killer. I keep telling people that.

speaker: BEN
line: But that could change, couldn't it? What do you got?

speaker: MATT
line: Bits and pieces. Russians. Triads. Yakuza. All funneling money through a man named Leland Owlsley.

speaker: BEN
line: The Wall Street guy? How'd you get all this?

speaker: MATT
line: How do you think?

speaker: BEN
line: So all you got is what you've beaten out of people? I can't print that without credible—

speaker: MATT
line: Detective Blake. I was at the hospital when he died.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah, they're saying you sent him on his way.

speaker: MATT
line: It was his partner, Hoffman. They both worked for Fisk. Blake gave Fisk up, before he went.

speaker: BEN
line: You get this on tape? Somebody else in the room to corroborate what he said? I need reliable sources. A bunch of "he said, she said" is not gonna put this guy away.

speaker: MATT
line: We don't need to put him away. Just drag him into the light. Give him nowhere to hide. Once the city knows who he is they'll tear him apart. And this is the guy at the top. You sure about that?

speaker: MATT
line: I'd bet my life on it.

speaker: BEN
line: You're betting mine now, too. Tell me everything you know.

speaker: BEN (VOICEOVER)
line: "'You get what you deserve.' It's an old saying. One that survived the years, because it's true. For the most part. But not for everyone. Some get more than they deserve. Because they believe they aren't like everyone else. That the rules, the ones people like me and you, the people that work and struggle to live our lives, just live, don't apply to them. That they can do anything and live happily ever after, while the rest of us suffer. They do this from the shadows. Shadows that we cast. With our indifference. With a pervasive lack of interest in anything that doesn't directly affect us, we, in the here and now. Or maybe it's just the shadow of weariness. Of how tired we are, struggling to claw our way back to a middle class that no longer exist, because of those who take more than they deserve. And they keep taking, until all that's left for the rest of us is a memory of how it used to be before the corporations and the bottom line decided we didn't matter anymore. But we do. You and I, the people of this city— we still matter. There's someone in Hell's Kitchen that doesn't share this belief. He's been among us for quite some time. You've never heard his name. You've never seen his face. He's stayed in the shadows. Because men like him, men that want to control our city, our lives, fear the light and what it reveals. This man must no longer be allowed to operate in the darkness. If he has nothing to hide, let him step forward."

speaker: FISK
line: I'm not very good at this, out, being in public. But I felt the need to speak up for this city that I love with all my heart. No one should have to live in fear. In fear of madmen who have no regard for who they injure.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: In fear of the Devil of Hell's Kitchen, who has inflicted untold pain and suffering. This masked terrorist and psychopaths of his kind, we must show them we will not bow down to their campaign of coercion and intimidation. We must stand up to them.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: As this man, my dearest friend, Leland Owlsley, a pillar in the financial community, stood up when he was recently assaulted. But this assault was for no other reason than to send me a message. A message warning me to stop.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: To give up my dream that I have for this city. A dream of a better place. A place for its citizens to feel safe. To feel pride. I tried to do this quietly, not wanting to draw attention. The last thing I wanted was for anyone close to me to become a target from those who do not share my dream. For those who will have this city stay exactly as it is, mired in poverty and crime. But I know now it was foolish to make that decision. That I can no longer do it alone. That I cannot keep living in the shadows afraid of the light. None of us can. None of us should be forced to. We must do this together. We must resist those who would have us live in fear.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: My name is Wilson Fisk. And together, we can make this city a better place.

speaker: THUG
line: Ahhh!

speaker: THUG
line: Ahh! Ahhh!

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Started to wonder if you'd ever turn up again.

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, I've, uh... been busy.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Hmm. Well, I'll be inside, you wanna take confession.

speaker: MATT
line: Uh, Father? I was wondering if I could take you up on that latte?

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Sugar?

speaker: MATT
line: No.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: So... what's on your mind, Matthew?

speaker: MATT
line: Wasn't that hard to find out. People still remember "Battlin' Jack" Murdock around these parts... and what happened to his son.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Seal of confession still applies, even over lattes. That what you're worried about.

speaker: MATT
line: Do you believe in the Devil, Father?

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: You mean... as a concept?

speaker: MATT
line: No. Do you believe he exists? In this world, among us.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: You want the short answer or the long one?

speaker: MATT
line: Just the truth.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: When I was in seminary... I was more studious than pious, more... skeptical than most of my peers. I had this notion... which I was more than willing to speak about, at length, to whoever I could corner... that the Devil... was inconsequential. Minor figure in the grand scheme.

speaker: MATT
line: Not very Catholic of you.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Uh-huh, yeah. In my defense, in the scriptures, the Hebrew word "Satan" actually means "adversary." It's applied to any antagonist. Angels and humans, serpents and kings. Medieval theologians reinterpreted those passages to be about a single monstrous enemy. And, in my youthful zeal, I was certain I knew why... propaganda. Played up to drive people into the church.

speaker: MATT
line: So you don't believe he exists.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Am I done talking?

speaker: MATT
line: Sorry.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Years later, I was in Rwanda... trying to help local churches provide aid and sanctuary to refugees. I'd become close with the village elder, Gahiji. He and his family had the respect of everybody, Hutu and Tutsi alike. He'd helped them all... through famines, disease. The militia liked to force Hutu villagers to murder their neighbors... with machetes. But nobody would raise a hand against Gahiji. They said, "Well... how can we kill such a holy man?" So the militia commander sent soldiers... with orders to cut his head off... in front of the entire village. Gahiji didn't try to put up a fight. Just asked for the chance to say goodbye to his family. By the time he was done, even the soldiers didn't wanna kill him. So they went to their commander and asked permission to shoot him. At least give him a quick death. The commander wanted to meet this man... who had won the respect of so many. He went to Gahiji... talked with him in his hut... for many hours. Then he dragged him out in front of his village and hacked him to pieces... along with his entire family. In that man who took Gahiji's life... I saw the Devil. So yes, Matthew... I believe he walks among us... taking many forms.

speaker: MATT
line: What if you could have stopped him... from ever hurting anyone again?

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: Stopped him how?

speaker: BEN
line: This doesn't change anything, Ben.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Except now we know who your king of diamonds is.

speaker: BEN
line: You see the news? Everything's changed. Fisk has gotten out in front of being dragged into the spotlight. My editor thinks he's the Second Coming. Hell, the whole city does.

speaker: KAREN
line: So, we just... We keep digging.

speaker: BEN
line: I've been doing that. Internet went from nothing on Fisk to filled with three-hanky stories about a poor little fat kid from Hell's Kitchen. Abandoned by his father when he was 12. Mother died a year later. Now look at him. Boot straps and a big dream.

speaker: KAREN
line: Somebody knows something. It's just a matter of asking the right people the right questions in the right tone of voice.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah, that's how you get yourself hurt.

speaker: FOGGY
line: That's what I keep telling them. Maybe they'll listen to you.

speaker: MATT
line: Ben Urich, Matt Murdock. Attorney at Why the Hell Bother.

speaker: BEN
line: Mr. Murdock.

speaker: MATT
line: Matt. My partner thinks we should be pursuing this through the legal system. A lot safer that way.

speaker: BEN
line: Well, why don't we all just crawl under the covers, then?

speaker: KAREN
line: No, Karen...

speaker: KAREN
line: Well, I'm sorry, but if Fisk is really behind everything that has happened, then we need to do something.

speaker: MATT
line: If we were the only ones after him, I'd tend to agree. Friend of yours came to see me the other night... the man in the mask.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Terrorist cop-killer.

speaker: BEN
line: Says he was framed.

speaker: FOGGY
line: I could say I'm Captain America, but it doesn't put wings on my head.

speaker: MATT
line: What did he want?

speaker: BEN
line: Same thing we do... expose Fisk. I printed this from a thumb drive he gave me.

speaker: KAREN
line: Oh, my God!

speaker: BEN
line: Told me Fisk was behind the bombings and shooting those cops... said he owns half the police... that they helped him take down the Russians.

speaker: KAREN
line: But I don't understand. If you have all of this, then...

speaker: MATT
line: Hearsay. Can't print any of it without corroboration, can you?

speaker: FOGGY
line: He could just be throwing smoke. I mean, he just killed Detective Blake.

speaker: BEN
line: Said Blake's partner Hoffman did it, probably on Fisk's orders. But yeah, it occurred to me.

speaker: MATT
line: You could talk to Hoffman.

speaker: BEN
line: Tried. He's in the wind. Or bottom of the river. Either way...

speaker: MATT
line: Sorry.

speaker: KAREN
line: Wait, what about the Union Allied money? Is there a way that we can tie it directly to Fisk?

speaker: BEN
line: Maybe. According to the Mask, a man named, uh, Leland Owlsley runs the books. But since getting roughed up by him, Owlsley's been surrounded by Fisk's security. Can't get anywhere near him. Same goes with, uh, James Wesley, the guy you said hired you to defend Healy.

speaker: KAREN
line: Look, the Mask came to Ben for help. And I don't care how rich Fisk is, nobody can totally erase their past. I mean, somewhere out there, there has to be a piece of paper, a witness... the truth.

speaker: FOGGY
line: What about Confederated Global? The suit that hired us to defend Healy standing right next to Fisk when he gave his big speech.

speaker: BEN
line: I looked into that. According to FCC filings, Confed Global's where Fisk gets most of his reported income.

speaker: MATT
line: All right, let's play this out. If Fisk is connected to Confed Global, that means he's involved in Westmeyer-Holt Contracting, which...

speaker: KAREN
line: Westmeyer-Holt is strong-arming tenants out of their rent-controlled apartments. Um, they were hired by a guy named Armand Tully.

speaker: BEN
line: The slumlord?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Landman and Zack say he's on vacation on an island that no one can pronounce, where they use coconuts as phones.

speaker: MATT
line: Another connection in the wind.

speaker: BEN
line: Westmeyer-Holt to Confed to Fisk. We pull that thread, see what it unravels.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Still not sure about this mask guy.

speaker: KAREN
line: He didn't hurt Ben and he didn't hurt me. I'll take the Devil of Hell's Kitchen over Fisk any day. Plus, he kicks ass. No, you should've seen the way that he was flipping around in the rain.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Well, if he's such a badass, why did he come to Ben? Why not just take Fisk down himself?

speaker: MATT
line: Maybe he knows there's some roads you can't come back from.

speaker: WESLEY
line: Our latest polls show your approval numbers rising... across political, ethnic and economic lines.

speaker: WESLEY
line: The 501 has been approved, so the PAC is actively making donations, and Senator Cherryh's office has asked for a meet.

speaker: FISK
line: Breakfast. Reject the first place they suggest. How about Detective Hoffman?

speaker: WESLEY
line: Our sources in IAB tell me he was supposed to give a follow-up statement about what happened at Metro-General. He never showed.

speaker: FISK
line: We need to put this behind us.

speaker: WESLEY
line: If he's still in the city, we'll find him.

speaker: FISK
line: If he isn't?

speaker: WESLEY
line: We'll still find him. It might just take a little longer.

speaker: FISK
line: And the man in the mask?

speaker: WESLEY
line: The authorities are motivated to shoot on sight... if they have the opportunity. He's not nearly as active as he has been in the past.

speaker: FISK
line: Maybe he's given up.

speaker: WESLEY
line: Maybe he's just choosing his targets more carefully.

speaker: FRANCIS
line: Hey, I said you need to wait outside.

speaker: FISK
line: It's all right, Francis. Thank you.

speaker: FISK
line: My apologies, Nobu-san. If I had known you were coming...

speaker: WESLEY
line: He doesn't care for the accommodations.

speaker: NOBU
line: Misspeak my words again... and I will have your tongue.

speaker: FISK
line: Wesley is just trying to be polite.

speaker: NOBU
line: The time for pleasantries... is at an end. I was promised a city block in return for my aid in your ventures.

speaker: FISK
line: There is a... a tenement in, um... this particular area... it has proven troublesome to vacate. But we have other blocks coming up if you...

speaker: INTERPRETER
line: This one.

speaker: FISK
line: I don't recall... guaranteeing a specific block. You'll need to be patient... or choose another.

speaker: NOBU
line: I am bound by certain requirements. Even I have those I must answer to. After the setback at the docks... I can afford no further disruptions. Do what you must, but do it quickly.

speaker: FISK
line: Wesley?

speaker: WESLEY
line: Regardless of how carefully it's handled, you're now the owner of record. The negative publicity could prove costly.

speaker: FISK
line: Then we'll blame the man in the mask. One more atrocity laid at his doorstep.

speaker: NOBU
line: I don't care what you must do. I have need of that property... or our alliance ends.

speaker: FISK
line: Consider it done.

speaker: MRS. CARDENAS
line: Who are you? What do you want?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Murdock and Nelson, how can I help?

speaker: FOGGY
line: What? When?

speaker: FOGGY
line: I'll drink to that.

speaker: KAREN
line: You think it was a coincidence? Elena decides to stay and fight, to rally what's left of her neighbors, and this happens.

speaker: MATT
line: Do you think Fisk had something to do with this?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Speak of the devil.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Hey, Josie, could you turn that up?

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: No, I never had the pleasure of meeting Ms. Cardenas. I only recently took possession of her building.

speaker: REPORTER (TV)
line: How do you respond to reports that you knew the tenement was unsafe?

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: That is accurate. That's why we offered a substantial sum to Ms. Cardenas and her neighbors to help them relocate. We should never let good people get swallowed up by this city. I mourn this woman's death. Didn't have to happen. It should've... Her passing is a symptom of a larger disease... infecting all of us.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: Disease of fear...

speaker: KAREN
line: Funeral home.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: ...fear of bombings, fear of cop killings.

speaker: KAREN
line: Hello?

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: Fear of a masked psychopath.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, that's me. Yeah, I need to make arrangements.

speaker: FISK (TV)
line: We shouldn't let people like that take our city from us. We need to stand together. Let them know that they will fail... because we believe we can make a difference. 'Cause they are cowards! Afraid of stepping out of the shadows. Afraid of standing up for people like Mrs. Cardenas. I'm sorry. I'm sorry.

speaker: REPORTER (TV)
line: Mr. Fisk, how does this affect the upcoming benefit?

speaker: WESLEY
line: That will be all. Thank you.

speaker: REPORTER (TV)
line: Mr. Fisk...

speaker: WESLEY
line: No more questions. Thank you very much.

speaker: REPORTER (TV)
line: What can we do about this psycho...

speaker: FOGGY
line: Jesus, he almost sounds like he means it.

speaker: MATT
line: I think he does.

speaker: KAREN
line: And he's calling the man in the mask a psycho? I hope they trace what happened to Elena right to his doorstep.

speaker: MATT
line: He'd never expose himself like that. Plus, half the force is probably in his pocket.

speaker: KAREN
line: Well, then, let's pray the Mask gets his hands on him. Knocks his goddamn head off.

speaker: MATT
line: You religious, Karen?

speaker: KAREN
line: My parents were. That's probably why I'm not. You?

speaker: MATT
line: Catholic.

speaker: KAREN
line: Does it help? With things like this?

speaker: MATT
line: Not today. I think I've had enough. Tell Foggy I'll see him in the morning.

speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah. Hey, Matt.

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah?

speaker: KAREN
line: If there is a God... and if he cares at all about... about any of us... Fisk will get what he deserves. You have to believe that.

speaker: MATT
line: I do.

speaker: MATT
line: Look at it. Where is he?

speaker: THUG
line: I don't know.

speaker: MATT
line: Tell me what you do know.

speaker: THUG
line: All right, all right, I'll tell you anything you want. Just, please, stop hurting me!

speaker: JUNKIE
line: Hey, you're real, you're... You're real...

speaker: MATT
line: Where'd you get the purse?

speaker: JUNKIE
line: What purse?

speaker: MATT
line: Lying? Bad idea.

speaker: JUNKIE
line: Please, stop! I'm... I'm sick. Okay! Okay, the purse! I'll tell you who snatched it...

speaker: MATT
line: Listen, I've hurt a lot of people tonight to get what I need to know. The asshole that killed Mrs. Cardenas shoots up at this address, likes cheap menthols. Thinks it covers the stench of his rotting teeth. It doesn't.

speaker: MATT
line: Who paid you?

speaker: JUNKIE
line: No, I don't, I don't...

speaker: MATT
line: Was it Fisk? Was it Fisk?

speaker: MATT
line: Was it Wilson Fisk?

speaker: JUNKIE
line: No, I don't know! Please, stop! Please!

speaker: MATT
line: Give me a reason to!

speaker: JUNKIE
line: I don't know their names. I don't! They found me. They took me to a warehouse on the water... Pier 81. I didn't wanna do it, man. I swear. I didn't wanna do it! But I was hurting. I was hurting, man.

speaker: MATT
line: Shut up! You're gonna turn yourself in... to Sergeant Brett Mahoney at the 15th Precinct. If you don't, I'll find you. And next time, I'm not gonna stop.

speaker: MATT
line: I didn't come here for you.

speaker: NOBU
line: But I am the one you have found.

speaker: MATT
line: You were at the docks with the boy.

speaker: NOBU
line: As were you... with the old fool. That was unexpected.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm not part of his war.

speaker: NOBU
line: Yet you aided him. And in the act, caused me displeasure.

speaker: MATT
line: Did Fisk send you? Is that why he paid that junkie to... A woman is dead, and for what? Just to lure me into some kind of a trap?

speaker: NOBU
line: You are here, are you not?

speaker: MATT
line: I knew no one was in the building. Made that mistake with the Russians once. Learned from it.

speaker: NOBU
line: But you did not know I was here.

speaker: MATT
line: No... you slowed your heart... lowered your body temperature.

speaker: NOBU
line: The old fool has taught you in our ways.

speaker: MATT
line: I told you I'm not with him.

speaker: NOBU
line: Yet you're still a warrior... deserving of a warrior's death.

speaker: MATT
line: I came here for Fisk. Guess I'll have to settle for you.

speaker: NOBU
line: I show you respect. You would be wise to return the courtesy.

speaker: MATT
line: You'll have to earn it.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Shit, sorry.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Hey, can I get another bottle over here? No, no, never mind, Josie. Hey, hey, Foggy. Foggy, I've had enough, and you have had... Way, way past that.

speaker: KAREN
line: It's a wake, Karen. People drink at wakes.

speaker: FOGGY
line: You don't need it. You know why? 'Cause it sucks.

speaker: KAREN
line: I know.

speaker: FOGGY
line: You speak Spanish. What's a good toast for the people that should... That should still...

speaker: KAREN
line: Hey. Hey, hey, hey.

speaker: FOGGY
line: I should have told her to take the money like Matt said.

speaker: KAREN
line: No, no, no, no, Foggy... it's not your fault, okay?

speaker: FOGGY
line: The Hell's Kitchen I grew up in was a real shithole. But it had a heart, you know?

speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Me and Matt... we learned the law... how to play by the rules. We were gonna help the people that we grew up with. Give 'em the same shot as the big boys like Fisk. It's all bullshit. It's all just... lies that we tell ourselves to make it through one more day.

speaker: KAREN
line: No, I don't... I don't believe that. I can't.

speaker: FOGGY
line: What are we supposed to do... against somebody that owns everything? Everyone? What can we do to somebody like that?

speaker: KAREN
line: The only thing you can... you make them pay.

speaker: NOBU
line: You have fought well.

speaker: NOBU
line: It is... not enough.

speaker: FISK
line: Thank you. Nobu was becoming an issue. I appreciate you... removing him from concern.

speaker: MATT
line: You... wanted me to do this.

speaker: FISK
line: In a perfect world, you would have taken each other out, but... it isn't a perfect world, is it? Not yet. To be honest... it took longer than I expected. Nobu didn't mind. He meditated for hours. I find it difficult to meditate. My mind, it won't quiet.

speaker: FISK
line: It's a character flaw, I suppose. We all have them. You, for instance. You've demonstrated an emotional weakness for children and women. I assumed that would extend to the elderly. So I baited the hook. Here you are.

speaker: MATT
line: You took her life... just to get my attention?

speaker: FISK
line: Nobu forced my hand in the matter. My options, they were limited by necessity. I took no pleasure in her passing.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm... gonna kill you.

speaker: FISK
line: Take your shot.

speaker: FISK
line: It's disappointing.

speaker: FISK
line: Wesley.

speaker: FISK
line: Put men on the dock. If they see the Mask, put a bullet in him.

speaker: WESLEY
line: What about Nobu?

speaker: FISK
line: Let him burn.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Matt! Come on, Matt. I need to talk to you, Matt.

speaker: FOGGY
line: We need to keep going, Matt. We gotta nail that bastard to the wall. We gotta make him pay... for Elena... for everything.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Matt? Are you okay in there? Matt? Matt!

speaker: FOGGY
line: Matt? It's me. I heard a crash. Not the fun, sexy-time kind, but... more of the... I've-fallen-and-I-can't-get-up variety. Matt?

speaker: FOGGY
line: If anyone who's in here is not supposed to be, I will mess you up. I'm not kidding.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Where's Matt? What'd you do to him? Shit.

speaker: KAREN
line: Matt?

speaker: MATT
line: Oh, God.

speaker: FOGGY (O.S.)
line: Wouldn't do that if I were you.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Then again, maybe I would. The hell do I know about Matt Murdock?

speaker: MATT
line: You stitched me up?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Nope. That was your nurse friend.

speaker: MATT
line: Claire?

speaker: FOGGY
line: You had me get a hold of her after you took a swing at me for trying to get you to the hospital.

speaker: MATT
line: I don't remember. Sorry.

speaker: FOGGY
line: She was hot, by the way. But I guess you already knew that, huh?

speaker: MATT
line: Foggy—

speaker: FOGGY
line: Just tell me one thing, Matt. Are you even really blind?

speaker: FOGGY
line: God damn it! Come on! Load. Load!

speaker: FOGGY
line: What?

speaker: MATT
line: Excuse me, is this room 312?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, who're you looking for?

speaker: MATT
line: Oh— uh, sorry.

speaker: FOGGY
line: What for? You're blind, right?

speaker: MATT
line: Uh, yeah, so they tell me. I hope that won't be a problem.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Why would it? Oh! You're... You're my roomie!

speaker: MATT
line: Uh, Matt Murdock.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Foggy Nelson. Wait, Matt Murdock? Are you— You're not from Hell's Kitchen, are you?

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, born and raised.

speaker: FOGGY
line: So am I! Yeah, I heard about you when you were a kid, what you did, saving that guy crossing the street.

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, I— I just did what anyone would have.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Bullshit. You are a hero.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm really not.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Come on! You got your peepers knocked out saving that old dude.

speaker: MATT
line: They didn't get knocked out.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Good, 'cause that would be a little freaky. But no offense.

speaker: MATT
line: Please, none taken. Uh— Most people dance around me like I'm made of glass. I hate that.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, you're just a guy, right? A really, really good-looking guy.

speaker: MATT
line: Oh, um...

speaker: FOGGY
line: I mean, girls must love that, the whole wounded, handsome duck thing. Am I right?

speaker: MATT
line: Right. Yeah, it's been known to happen.

speaker: FOGGY
line: This is gonna be awesome!

speaker: MATT
line: What is?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Me as your wingman! You're gonna open up a whole caliber of women I've only dreamed of. A lot! We're gonna be like Maverick and Goose!

speaker: MATT
line: Okay.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Oh, shit! Yes. I'm in!

speaker: MATT
line: In what?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Punjabi. I got the last spot.

speaker: MATT
line: You're taking Punjabi?

speaker: FOGGY
line: It's spoken by 130 million people. I'd like to know what they're saying.

speaker: MATT
line: That's the only reason?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Well, yeah. I mean, why else would I learn it?

speaker: MATT
line: I don't know, a girl, maybe?

speaker: FOGGY
line: See? This is what I'm talking about. Me and you— Maverick and Goose, no secrets.

speaker: MATT
line: Goose died and he was married.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Details. Hey, do you know a good place to get a cup of coffee on campus?

speaker: MATT
line: No.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Well, lucky for you, I do. And it's filled with luscious coeds. Shall we?

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, lead the way.

speaker: FOGGY
line: So, you can see.

speaker: MATT
line: That's not— You're not— Are you even listening to what I'm saying?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, world on fire, I got it. But you can see, right?

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, in a manner of speaking. But I—

speaker: FOGGY
line: No! No manner! How many fingers am I holding up?

speaker: MATT
line: One.

speaker: FOGGY
line: All these years, I actually felt sorry for you.

speaker: MATT
line: I didn't ask for that. I never— I never asked for that.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, I didn't ask to be lied to. I thought we were friends.

speaker: MATT
line: We are.

speaker: FOGGY
line: You've lied to me, Matt, since the day we met.

speaker: MATT
line: What did you expect me to say, Foggy? "Hi, I'm Matt. I got some chemicals splashed in my eyes when I was a kid that gave me heightened senses."

speaker: FOGGY
line: Well, maybe not lead with that.

speaker: MATT
line: I didn't even tell my dad after it happened.

speaker: FOGGY
line: But you told that nurse, Claire.

speaker: MATT
line: Because I didn't have a choice. She found me in a dumpster, all right? Half dead. She didn't— She didn't tell you?

speaker: FOGGY
line: She wouldn't say anything about all this. She seemed nice.

speaker: MATT
line: She is.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Did you blow up those buildings? Shoot those cops?

speaker: MATT
line: You really even need to ask that?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, I think I do.

speaker: MATT
line: It was Fisk. It was all Fisk.

speaker: FOGGY
line: He did this to you?

speaker: MATT
line: He and Nobu.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Nobu?

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, I think he's some kind of ninja.

speaker: FOGGY
line: A ninja.

speaker: MATT
line: I think.

speaker: FOGGY
line: What are you doing, Matt? You're a lawyer. You're supposed to be helping people.

speaker: MATT
line: I am.

speaker: FOGGY
line: In a mask! Do you know what they call that? A vigilante. Someone who acts outside of the law.

speaker: PHONE
line: Karen. Karen. Karen. Karen. Karen.

speaker: MATT
line: Foggy, Foggy, Foggy.

speaker: FOGGY
line: She deserves to know.

speaker: MATT
line: You can't tell her, Foggy, please.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Is this what you do? When we call, trying to get you to come out for drinks? Trying to find you when bombs are going off and we're worried?

speaker: MATT
line: You just hit ignore?

speaker: FOGGY
line: No.

speaker: FOGGY
line: It's her again.

speaker: MATT
line: Please, Foggy.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Hey.

speaker: KAREN (PHONE)
line: Hey. I tried calling Matt. Where are you guys?

speaker: FOGGY
line: We're at his place.

speaker: KAREN
line: Is everything okay?

speaker: FOGGY
line: No, Matt was— Matt was in an accident.

speaker: KAREN
line: Oh, my God. What happened?

speaker: FOGGY
line: He was in a car accident.

speaker: KAREN
line: Matt was driving?

speaker: FOGGY
line: No, he, um— He got hit.

speaker: KAREN
line: Well, is he all right? Look, I— I'm coming over.

speaker: FOGGY
line: No, stay at the office. We need you there. There's nothing you can do here.

speaker: KAREN
line: Okay. Foggy...

speaker: FOGGY
line: I got this, Karen.

speaker: KAREN
line: I'll call you if we need anything.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Thank you. Screw you. I just lied to somebody that I care about. I want to know everything. And don't you leave a damn thing out.

speaker: GAO
line: I have never seen you, absent your man by your side.

speaker: FISK
line: No need for a translator now.

speaker: GAO
line: Or pretenses. There was a snake, in the village where I was raised who mistook an elephant as prey. It died with its jaws wide clenched around no more than the elephant's foot, betrayed by ambition.

speaker: FISK
line: Am I the snake or the elephant?

speaker: GAO
line: What happened to Nobu was unfortunate.

speaker: FISK
line: I asked for a warrior to eliminate the Masked Man. He chose to take it upon himself.

speaker: GAO
line: He is a man of pride. Something well known to you.

speaker: FISK
line: What's done is done.

speaker: GAO
line: And the man in the mask, you have found his body?

speaker: FISK
line: No. Yet Nobu's clan prepare his for what is to come.

speaker: GAO
line: They are distracted. But their memories and their knives are forever sharp.

speaker: FISK
line: Is that why you wanted to meet? To warn me of what I already know?

speaker: GAO
line: I only sought to pose a question. How long before your ambition turns to me?

speaker: FISK
line: You always possessed what the others did not. My respect.

speaker: GAO
line: Perhaps. Yet you are not the man who came to me with a dream for this city. He was of a singular mind. Yours now is pulled in two directions by longings of the heart.

speaker: FISK
line: Vanessa is not a distraction.

speaker: GAO
line: Yet you keep her close, even when her presence endangers her.

speaker: FISK
line: I know what I'm doing.

speaker: GAO
line: Then you are more foolish than I thought. My path is set. I leave this city soon. I would not stay for all your iron and all your gold. Good luck, Wilson Fisk. You will need it in what is to come.

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: Mr. Nelson, care to share with the class?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Uh, yes, Professor. I was just, uh... discussing the merits of the case with my associate here.

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: Your associate being Mr. Murdock?

speaker: MATT
line: Actually, Professor, we were debating whether the defendant's Fourth Amendment rights were violated.

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: And what did you conclude?

speaker: MATT
line: That the search was illegal. The police didn't have probable cause.

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: Interesting. Mr. Nelson, do you agree?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Absolutely. The fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine clearly applies here.

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: Very good. Both of you. See me after class.

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: You two make a good team. Ever thought about practicing together?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Us? Really?

speaker: PROFESSOR
line: You complement each other. Mr. Murdock has the instincts, and you, Mr. Nelson, have the work ethic to back them up. Think about it.

speaker: MATT
line: Stick found me when I was a kid. He trained me, taught me how to fight, how to control my abilities.

speaker: FOGGY
line: This Stick guy, he made you into what you are?

speaker: MATT
line: He gave me the tools. But I chose this path myself.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Why? Why would you choose this?

speaker: MATT
line: Because someone had to. The system doesn't work for everyone, Foggy. You know that. We've seen it firsthand.

speaker: FOGGY
line: So you decided to take the law into your own hands?

speaker: MATT
line: I decided to do what the law couldn't.

speaker: FOGGY
line: That's not your call to make, Matt.

speaker: MATT
line: Then whose is it? The cops who are on Fisk's payroll? The judges he's bought? The system is broken, Foggy.

speaker: FOGGY
line: So you fix it by beating people up?

speaker: MATT
line: I stop bad people from doing bad things. That's all I'm trying to do.

speaker: FOGGY
line: No, I don't know shit. Not about this. I mean, how— Okay, so you get these whatever-you-call-thems when you're a kid. How do you go from that to what you're doing now?

speaker: MATT
line: When I was a kid, before the accident— I'd lay awake at night listening to the sirens. I liked to put stories to them. Trying to figure out what they were for, ambulance or cops, robbery or fire. I don't know, just a stupid game. But after I lost my sight, after my abilities developed, I realized how many sirens there actually were— how much this city suffered every single night.

speaker: FOGGY
line: You've been running around doing this since you were a kid?

speaker: MATT
line: No. I— I tried not to fight— to make my dad proud. To— to block it out. The sirens, the pain, the fear, all strangling Hell's Kitchen. For years, I buried my head and turned away. Then one night— right after we quit Landman and Zack— I heard it.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Heard what?

speaker: MATT
line: A little girl crying in her bed, in a building down the block. Her father liked to go to her room late at night when his wife was asleep.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Oh, Jesus.

speaker: MATT
line: I called Child Services like you're supposed to. But the mom, she wouldn't believe it. Said it wasn't true. And the dad, he was smart. He made sure what he did, how he did it, didn't leave a mark. The law couldn't do anything to help that little girl. But I could. I knew his routine. Waited till he was alone.

speaker: MATT
line: You touch your daughter again, and I will know.

speaker: MATT
line: He spent the next month in a hospital, eating through a straw. And I never slept better.

speaker: FOGGY
line: You say all this, like one day you'd just had it with how things are. But to do what you do— you had to keep training, all those years since that Stick guy, knowing you would do something like this. Maybe it isn't only about justice, Matt. Maybe it's about you having an excuse to hit someone. Maybe you just can't stop yourself.

speaker: MATT
line: I don't want to stop.

speaker: BEN
line: You're very pretty.

speaker: KAREN
line: Thank you.

speaker: BEN
line: Looks like you've got yourself an admirer.

speaker: KAREN
line: All the people here, all the years that they've lived, there must be so many stories.

speaker: BEN
line: Only thing we have, everything said and done. No buildings named after us, fancy inheritances to leave behind, just the stories those who were close to us tell to keep us alive. Even if it's just in memory.

speaker: KAREN
line: Well, maybe that's enough.

speaker: KAREN
line: Hey, um, why don't we talk to somebody that actually lives here? See what it's really like.

speaker: BEN
line: All right, let's get a— Let's get an attendant or somebody.

speaker: KAREN
line: Or we could just knock. See?

speaker: BEN
line: Karen.

speaker: VOICE
line: Come in.

speaker: KAREN
line: She said, "Come in."

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: Is it time?

speaker: KAREN
line: Time for what?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: You know what. You bring it before I go to bed every night. Oh. I don't know you, do I?

speaker: BEN
line: Oh— Uh, no.

speaker: KAREN
line: We uh, we just— We wanted to ask you some questions.

speaker: BEN
line: About how you like it at Saint Benezet.

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: It's very nice, isn't it?

speaker: KAREN
line: It is. How long have you been here?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: A while now. Ever since my husband passed. Are you two married?

speaker: BEN
line: No. Well, I am, but not to her.

speaker: KAREN
line: No, I'm single. Uh, Mrs. Vistain...

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: Is it time?

speaker: BEN
line: Uh— We're sorry to bother you, ma'am. We should go.

speaker: KAREN
line: Mrs. Vistain, um, your husband— Was that your first marriage?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: Arthur? Lord, no, he was my third. Kept his name, thought it sounded like royalty. I always loved that. Martin was my second. Such a beautiful man. But confused by other men.

speaker: KAREN
line: Oh, um— Your first marriage— who was that to?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: He tried so hard, but he drank, you know. I didn't. Never touched a drop. Not once, no.

speaker: KAREN
line: And, uh— did you have any children with your first husband?

speaker: BEN
line: Karen...

speaker: KAREN
line: Just let her answer. Mrs. Vistain?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: He's such a good boy. Comes to see me every weekend. He's gentle, sweet. Not like his father.

speaker: KAREN
line: And what's his name? Your son?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: Wilson.

speaker: BEN
line: Fisk? Wilson Fisk?

speaker: MRS. VISTAIN
line: I haven't used that name since— It wasn't his fault. His father, he was— Wilson just wanted him to stop. It wasn't his fault, what he did.

speaker: KAREN
line: Mrs. Vistain, what did your son do?

speaker: FISK
line: There are those that question why a man such as myself, a man who treasures his privacy, would willingly subject himself to the public eye. I question the man who wouldn't step forward when his city, his heart, is in such a time of need. With your help, we can ensure that everyone that was affected by the recent attacks, and all who call Hell's Kitchen their home, will see a brighter day. I thank you, and please enjoy your evening.

speaker: VANESSA
line: That was beautiful.

speaker: FISK
line: That word is meant for only you tonight.

speaker: FISK
line: Thank you for coming. Thank you so much. Of course, thank you. It's a pleasure to see you again. Nice to see you. Thank you so much for the donation. It means the world to me, and to my organization. Yeah, mmm-hmm.

speaker: LELAND
line: I haven't been in a room with so many deep pockets since the junk bond days.

speaker: FISK
line: Leland, I was starting to worry.

speaker: LELAND
line: It's taken care of.

speaker: FISK
line: Appreciate it.

speaker: LELAND
line: Yeah, great. So, does anybody need a drink as bad as I do?

speaker: VANESSA
line: Yes, please.

speaker: SENATOR CHERRYH
line: It was a hell of a speech, Fisk. You ever think about running for office?

speaker: FISK
line: I'll leave that to people like you, Senator.

speaker: SENATOR CHERRYH
line: That's a good answer. You, um— got a minute to talk about that zoning issue?

speaker: FISK
line: Yes, of course. I'll be back in a minute.

speaker: VANESSA
line: I didn't vote for Senator Cherryh last election.

speaker: GUEST
line: Thank you so much.

speaker: WESLEY
line: Few people did. But he still won.

speaker: VANESSA
line: He said it was because of the advice he got from Van Lunt and his crackpot astrologer, if you can believe that.

speaker: WESLEY
line: Van Lunt?

speaker: VANESSA
line: Yeah, he's the guy who owns this mausoleum. Ask me, has more to do with Cherryh having his fingers in all the right holes.

speaker: LELAND
line: Somebody can't hold his liquor.

speaker: LELAND
line: What the hell is this?

speaker: FISK
line: Wesley, get the car. We need to leave now.

speaker: FISK
line: Vanessa!

speaker: FISK
line: Christ! Somebody get a doctor here! Somebody get a doctor! Vanessa? Vanessa! Vanessa!

speaker: FOGGY
line: You're going to get yourself killed, you keep this up. You know that, right?

speaker: MATT
line: I can take care of myself.

speaker: FOGGY
line: What about the rest of us? Me, Karen— we're a part of this now, because of you. And we didn't get a say in that.

speaker: MATT
line: What do you think's gonna happen if I give up now, Foggy? Who's going to stop Fisk?

speaker: FOGGY
line: Oh, I don't know— the law?

speaker: MATT
line: Tell that to Elena. If you could have put on a mask and prevented what happened to her— you telling me you wouldn't have?

speaker: FOGGY
line: It's not fair, Matt.

speaker: MATT
line: We don't live in a world that's fair. We live in this one. And I'm doing everything I can to make it a better place.

speaker: FOGGY
line: "A better place." That kind of sounds like what Fisk keeps saying.

speaker: MATT
line: Don't say that. Don't twist it around.

speaker: FOGGY
line: You tried to kill him, Matt. You told me yourself. How is that any different than the way he solves his problems?

speaker: MATT
line: I made a mistake. I know that.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Misspelling "Hanukkah" is a mistake. Attempted murder is a little something else. You ever stop to think what would happen if you went to jail? Or worse? You really think that anyone would believe that I didn't know what you were doing? That Karen didn't know?

speaker: MATT
line: This city needs me in that mask, Foggy.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Maybe you're right. Maybe it does. But I don't. I only ever needed my friend. I wouldn't have kept this from you, Matt. Not from you.

speaker: MATT
line: You don't know that. You don't know that.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah, I do.

speaker: MATT
line: Foggy, wait. Foggy.

speaker: FOGGY
line: I worry about you, it's all I'm saying.

speaker: MATT
line: Foggy, I'm fine.

speaker: JOSIE
line: Don't look fine.

speaker: FOGGY
line: See, Josie's worried about you too.

speaker: JOSIE
line: I wouldn't go that far.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Gotta be more careful.

speaker: MATT
line: I know. I know.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Tripping and falling taking out the trash. You got to get someone to do that for you.

speaker: MATT
line: Come on, I just need to be more careful, like you said.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Done! Run your feelers over this little beauty.

speaker: MATT
line: What is it, a napkin?

speaker: FOGGY
line: No, my friend, this is our future.

speaker: MATT
line: Huh, feels like a napkin.

speaker: FOGGY
line: It's a drawing of a sign. "Nelson and Murdock, Attorneys At Law."

speaker: MATT
line: You, uh— You really want to do this?

speaker: FOGGY
line: No, I'm pissing my pants. There is actual urine in my trousers. But I trust you. You think this is what we should be doing then I'm with you. For better or worse.

speaker: MATT
line: Sounds like we're getting married.

speaker: FOGGY
line: This is way more important than a civil union! Come on, we're gonna be business partners. We're gonna share everything with each other. Our thoughts, our dreams, bills, crushing debt—

speaker: MATT
line: There is no one I'd rather be doing this with, buddy. Seriously.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Me, too, pal. Now raise your damn glass, 'cause I'm gonna clink the hell out of it. Nelson and Murdock, Attorneys at Law.

speaker: MATT
line: Nelson and Murdock.

speaker: DOCTOR
line: We need a doctor! Now! Let's get a gurney out here!

speaker: NURSE
line: What happened?

speaker: FISK
line: She drank something.

speaker: DOCTOR
line: What did she ingest? I need you to be specific.

speaker: WESLEY
line: I have no idea. It was at the Van Lunt building, the benefit.

speaker: FISK
line: There were others— Uh, I had a glass in my hand. Do I need to be checked out?

speaker: DOCTOR
line: How long's she been unconscious?

speaker: WESLEY
line: Twenty minutes. Maybe a little longer.

speaker: FISK
line: Place is a rat hole.

speaker: WESLEY
line: It was the closest ER. I reached out to Dr. Rosenberg. He's on the jet.

speaker: DOCTOR
line: Pupils are sluggish. I need an intubation tray, stat! Let's start 1,000 cc's of Ringer's lactate to KVO until we know what's going on. Insert a Foley catheter—

speaker: NURSE
line: Hemodialysis and gastric lavage?

speaker: DOCTOR
line: I need a tox screen, liver and kidney function, coagulation tests. I'll call ICU for a bed.

speaker: DOCTOR
line: You said there were others, how many?

speaker: WESLEY
line: Uh, four or five maybe.

speaker: FISK
line: Are you sure someone shouldn't be looking at me?

speaker: DOCTOR
line: We'll have a nurse come check you out.

speaker: FISK
line: I'm coming with her.

speaker: DOCTOR
line: I'm sorry, we can't have you in there, sir.

line: Sorry, just, I, uh... Just had a... a rough night.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: You and I should not drink.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah. Yeah, I'm thinking about giving it up, moving on to the hard stuff.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Narcotics? Deal me in.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: You don't seem like the type.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah, I smoked a doobie once. Made me drool.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: A doobie...

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Weed, pot, the Mary Jane. Whatever the kids are calling it these days.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: I'm not sure that's, uh, considered hard anymore. At least, not according to Denver, anyway.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: The times they are a-changin'.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Yeah. Yeah. So, you coming back to the office?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: I just needed to pick up a few things.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Wait, Foggy. Let's not do this right now. It's not a good time.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Is it ever gonna be?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: I don't know.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: That's not really an answer.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Best one I got. Whatever's going on between you and Matt, it would be really nice not to be alone here, you know?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: I know. What you said last night, you were right. No matter what's going on between me and Matt... that doesn't change anything with Fisk. I'm gonna keep digging. You can't just run around killing people and call yourself a human being. He's gonna pay for what he's done, just like you said.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Do we still have a copy of all that stuff Ben gave us, from the... the man in the mask?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah, uh, I think so. What are you gonna do with it?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Honestly, I have no idea.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: So, you, uh... you don't think the Mask is a terrorist anymore?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: I don't understand what he is. But no, I don't think he's a terrorist.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: It's a start, I guess. Look, I know things are... weird. But I'm still around. You need me, just call.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: You gonna pick up this time?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah, I'll pick up. Might not seem like it, but everything's gonna be all right.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: How can you be sure?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Because I have to be. Ease off the booze, stay away from the Mary Jane.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: FOGGY
line: Will do.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: Well, that wasn't awkward. What are you doing here so late? Or early or whatever it is?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Um... couldn't sleep.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: Lot of that going around. Seems like it's the only thing we still all have in common.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: I'm sorry, Karen.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: For which part?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: All of it, pretty much. You want coffee?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: Yeah, please.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: You know, he thinks he got her killed... Elena.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: He didn't.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: You wanna try telling him that? Oh, right, that... that would be if you two were still speaking to each other.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: It's his choice.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Only if you let it be. You know, I'm starting to feel like I made a mistake... coming to work here.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: Do you want to leave?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: No. This is my home. You and Foggy, you're the only good things in my life right now.

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: MATT
line: Karen, did something happen?

location: MURDOCK & NELSON LAW OFFICE - LATE NIGHT
speaker: KAREN
line: Yes. The world fell apart. Didn't you notice?

speaker: VANESSA
line: Wilson?

speaker: FISK
line: You... Don't speak. I'll get the doctor.

speaker: VANESSA
line: Why... why am... why am I here?

speaker: FISK
line: It was the benefit. Something was in your drink. But it was my fault. I should have known, the way things are, that someone would try to get to me. And I'm sorry. You were caught in the middle.

speaker: VANESSA
line: Someone tries to kill you and you're the one apologizing?

speaker: FISK
line: You almost died, Vanessa, because of me... because of who I am. I made arrangements. When you're able to be moved, you'll be... taken out of the country.

speaker: VANESSA
line: Are you coming with me?

speaker: FISK
line: Then... I think I'll stay where I am.

speaker: VANESSA
line: I need to keep you safe.

speaker: FISK
line: Is that really all you need?

speaker: VANESSA
line: I was being selfish... believing that I could have this... that there would be no consequences.

speaker: FISK
line: I knew being with you would be... complicated. I made that choice. One I still make.

speaker: VANESSA
line: Find who did this to us and make them understand.

speaker: FISK
line: Understand what?

speaker: VANESSA
line: That they could never take you away from me.

speaker: FRANCIS
line: Sir?

speaker: FISK
line: Not now.

speaker: VANESSA
line: Go. Go.

speaker: FISK
line: No, it can wait.

speaker: VANESSA
line: I'm still here. I'm not leaving.

speaker: FISK
line: I'll make them suffer for what they've done.

speaker: VANESSA
line: I expect nothing less.

speaker: FISK
line: Sorry, sir.

speaker: FRANCIS
line: What is it?

speaker: FISK
line: They've located him.

speaker: FRANCIS
line: And where is he?

speaker: MAN
line: Sir, excuse me, stop. I can't let you go in...

speaker: LELAND
line: Get your hands off me, moron. He called me.

speaker: LELAND
line: Oh, shit.

speaker: FISK
line: Look what they did, Leland. Look what they did to him.

speaker: LELAND
line: What happened?

speaker: FRANCIS
line: He got a call last night at the hospital.

speaker: LELAND
line: From who?

speaker: FRANCIS
line: I don't know. He asked for the keys to the SUV and my gun.

speaker: FISK
line: And you let him leave? Alone?

speaker: FRANCIS
line: He ordered me to stay. He wanted as many men on you as possible.

speaker: LELAND
line: Whoa, Wilson! Wilson!

speaker: FISK
line: He's my friend! He's... my... friend!

speaker: LELAND
line: May... maybe this isn't the best time to be beating your men to death. He... he did what he was told. I think they call that loyalty, or something.

speaker: FISK
line: Clean him up.

speaker: LELAND
line: First, the attack at the benefit, now this?

speaker: LELAND
line: Somebody's not happy. Nobu's accounts... are they still active?

speaker: LELAND
line: Yeah, but nothing's been touched since he went up in smoke.

speaker: FISK
line: And Gao?

speaker: LELAND
line: You think this is her?

speaker: FISK
line: No, my money's on the Japanese. Maybe they found out about your little bonfire with their boss.

speaker: LELAND
line: You can go now, Leland.

speaker: LELAND
line: Okay. But... whatever war you're thinking about starting... don't lose sight of the end game. Once Senator Cherryh has cleared the last of the zoning issues, you can tear down the rest of Hell's Kitchen and build your better tomorrow. It's a shame not everybody'll be there to see it, but... shit happens.

speaker: FISK
line: Find out who did this to... to Vanessa and to Wesley.

speaker: LELAND
line: I'll see what I can shake loose. Just remember, uh... wind blows the hardest the closer you get to the mountaintop.

speaker: BEN
line: You like making an entrance, don't you?

speaker: MATT
line: I need information.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah? Haven't heard anything about a man in a mask beating on bad guys lately. Thought maybe you'd quit on us.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm still here.

speaker: BEN
line: Somebody get a piece of you?

speaker: MATT
line: We went the distance, it's all that matters.

speaker: BEN
line: "Went the distance," huh? Sound like a boxer.

speaker: MATT
line: Always a reporter.

speaker: BEN
line: Hey, it's what I do. Why I'm here.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah, I've seen this around... all over the city. Heroin, pure like you've never seen. Call it "Steel Serpent" on the streets.

speaker: MATT
line: The man I took that off of murdered Elena Cardenas.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah, I heard about that.

speaker: MATT
line: He was working for Fisk. Vladimir Ranskahov, before he died, he said Fisk arranged access to the Chinese and their drugs.

speaker: BEN
line: Russians got wiped out.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm not interested in the Russians.

speaker: BEN
line: You're thinking about making a move on the triads now?

speaker: MATT
line: Russians were distribution, right?

speaker: BEN
line: That's what I hear.

speaker: MATT
line: With them out the way, there's an awful lot of money lying on the table.

speaker: BEN
line: You think Fisk picked up distribution?

speaker: MATT
line: Like I said, a lot of money. And I'm guessing tearing down Hell's Kitchen isn't cheap. Interrupting the cash flow may... slow him down.

speaker: BEN
line: Doubt if it'll stop him.

speaker: MATT
line: No... but it might knock him off balance. Get him mad, maybe enough to make a mistake big enough to matter.

speaker: BEN
line: I got something I'm working on, might help push that bald prick over the edge.

speaker: MATT
line: No, I want you to keep your head down, until this is over.

speaker: BEN
line: My head's fine where it's at.

speaker: MATT
line: Oh, yeah? Vladimir's brother probably thought the same.

speaker: BEN
line: Point taken.

speaker: MATT
line: The Chinese, who's the man at the top?

speaker: BEN
line: Isn't one, it's a woman. Never got her name.

speaker: MATT
line: Any idea where I can find her?

speaker: BEN
line: If I did, it'd be on the front page. The Russian that Blake shot in interrogation, he was heading to a building down in Chinatown when we picked him up. Place on Hester. Maybe start there.

speaker: MATT
line: Thank you, Ben.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah. You be careful.

speaker: MATT
line: What is this?

speaker: GAO
line: I have been waiting for you.

speaker: MATT
line: You speak English.

speaker: GAO
line: When I choose to.

speaker: MATT
line: These people... they're all blind.

speaker: GAO
line: Yes.

speaker: MATT
line: Why?

speaker: GAO
line: To spare them the distractions of this world.

speaker: MATT
line: You blinded them?

speaker: GAO
line: They blinded themselves. An act of faith.

speaker: MATT
line: Faith in what? Your drugs?

speaker: GAO
line: In something beyond the distractions of your world.

speaker: MATT
line: You're working with Fisk.

speaker: GAO
line: I have a business arrangement, yes.

speaker: MATT
line: Tell me about it.

speaker: GAO
line: Why should I?

speaker: MATT
line: Because I can make you.

speaker: GAO
line: Can you?

speaker: MATT
line: What are you?

speaker: GAO
line: Something you're not ready to face.

speaker: MATT
line: You're going to tell me about Fisk.

speaker: GAO
line: No. I'm leaving this city. My business here is concluded.

speaker: MATT
line: Not until you tell me what I need to know.

speaker: GAO
line: I have no interest in your crusade against Wilson Fisk.

speaker: MATT
line: Then you won't mind telling me how to stop him.

speaker: GAO
line: You assume you can.

speaker: MATT
line: I have to try.

speaker: GAO
line: Why? What is he to you?

speaker: MATT
line: He's destroying this city. Hurting innocent people.

speaker: GAO
line: And you believe you're different from him?

speaker: MATT
line: I don't kill people.

speaker: GAO
line: Yet. But you've thought about it. Many times.

speaker: MATT
line: That's different.

speaker: GAO
line: Is it? You're both men driven by darkness. The only difference is that he has embraced it while you... you struggle against it.

speaker: MATT
line: I'm nothing like him.

speaker: GAO
line: Tell yourself that if it brings you comfort. But you know the truth. You feel it in your bones.

speaker: MATT
line: Just tell me about Fisk.

speaker: GAO
line: Wilson Fisk is not your only concern. There are forces at work in this city that you cannot comprehend. Things beyond your understanding.

speaker: MATT
line: Try me.

speaker: GAO
line: You come from a place far from the light. So does Wilson Fisk. But you both seek to return there, don't you? Each in your own way.

speaker: MATT
line: What does that mean?

speaker: GAO
line: It means you're more alike than you wish to admit. And that may be your undoing.

speaker: MATT
line: What's happening?

speaker: GAO
line: My departure. Goodbye, masked man. We will not meet again.

speaker: MATT
line: All those people... You took their eyes.

speaker: GAO (VOICEOVER)
line: No. They blinded themselves.

speaker: MATT
line: Why would they do that?

speaker: GAO (VOICEOVER)
line: Because they have faith.

speaker: MATT
line: In you and your drugs?

speaker: GAO (VOICEOVER)
line: In something beyond the distractions of your world. You have taken that from them. Now, they will have nothing.

speaker: MATT
line: You're gonna tell me about Fisk.

speaker: MATT
line: Get these people out of here.

speaker: MATT
line: You're going to be okay. Come on.

speaker: BRETT
line: Police! Don't you move! Hands, let me see your hands! Hands! Slowly, slowly. You're the guy. The one that killed Blake and shot those cops!

speaker: MATT
line: I did not kill Detective Blake, or shoot those cops.

speaker: MATT
line: Blake and Hoffman were dirty. Working for Wilson Fisk. Along with a lot of others in your precinct. I'm not the bad guy.

speaker: BRETT
line: Then what are you?

speaker: BRETT
line: Officer down. Call it in now.

speaker: LELAND
line: You're late.

speaker: GAO
line: Apologies, I was detained by unfortunate events.

speaker: LELAND
line: You speak English now?

speaker: GAO
line: The need for illusion has passed.

speaker: LELAND
line: That have anything to do with why you're late?

speaker: GAO
line: The man in the mask.

speaker: LELAND
line: The heroin?

speaker: GAO
line: Lost in the flames.

speaker: LELAND
line: So, bring more in.

speaker: GAO
line: My interest here has never been about heroin, Leland. That was borne of convenience, and it is no longer so.

speaker: LELAND
line: Do what you want. I could honestly care less. If he finds out what we did... this isn't gonna matter.

speaker: GAO
line: Wilson suspects?

speaker: LELAND
line: Not yet, but that could change. We knew the risk, and the reward, if his woman were to be removed as a distraction.

speaker: GAO
line: I should've just had her shot.

speaker: LELAND
line: Well, he still believes that the poison was meant for him, yes?

speaker: GAO
line: Far as I know.

speaker: LELAND
line: Then our path was the correct one.

speaker: GAO
line: Except for the part where she's not dead, sure.

speaker: LELAND
line: The woman is stronger than assumed.

speaker: GAO
line: Yeah, she's a real mule. What about Wesley?

speaker: LELAND
line: What about him?

speaker: GAO
line: He's dead. Found in a basement, couple holes in his chest. Thought maybe that was you.

speaker: LELAND
line: No... he had never shown me discourtesy.

speaker: LELAND
line: So, what's our play here?

speaker: GAO
line: The wheel constantly turns. We must adapt to its position, or be crushed beneath it.

speaker: LELAND
line: What? Where the hell are you going?

speaker: GAO
line: I will visit my homeland and reflect upon the future.

speaker: LELAND
line: Home? China?

speaker: GAO
line: It is a considerable distance farther.

speaker: GAO
line: We shall not speak again.

speaker: LELAND
line: Fine, go! You think I don't have a fallback? You think I got this far without looking at my own damn tea leaves, huh? What, you think I'm gonna just...

speaker: DORIS
line: Those for me?

speaker: BEN
line: Till I get a better girl.

speaker: DORIS
line: You can't get a better girl.

speaker: BEN
line: Don't I know it.

speaker: DORIS
line: Ah... Mmm. Hard day?

speaker: BEN
line: I've had better.

speaker: DORIS
line: You've had worse, too. Am I right?

speaker: BEN
line: Usually are.

speaker: DORIS
line: I have my moments. Not many lately, but...

speaker: BEN
line: Let's go to Paris... like we always talked about.

speaker: DORIS
line: While we're still young.

speaker: BEN
line: Ooh, you want to run away together?

speaker: DORIS
line: Or just... run away?

speaker: BEN
line: How long we been together?

speaker: DORIS
line: Don't remember a time when we weren't. Got to know that look in your eye early on. Ben, there's a story eating at you... one you know you gotta tell.

speaker: BEN
line: Not that simple.

speaker: DORIS
line: Telling the truth is never simple... or easy. Why, only the best of us ever really try.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah. Ellison thinks it's a pile of shit.

speaker: DORIS
line: You straighten him out.

speaker: BEN
line: We got into it. He let me go.

speaker: DORIS
line: Good... You never needed that man. You never needed that paper. You only ever needed a story. Go tell it.

speaker: BEN
line: How? Shout it from the rooftops?

speaker: DORIS
line: You know there's this thing called the Internet, right? Reach a whole lot of folks, huh? More than you ever could at the Bulletin.

speaker: BEN
line: The Internet's all gossip, noise.

speaker: DORIS
line: So, cut through it. The world needs Ben Urich to tell the truth... any way he can.

speaker: KAREN
line: You quit?

speaker: BEN
line: Not exactly the way it went.

speaker: KAREN
line: Oh... I'm sorry.

speaker: BEN
line: Don't be. Bulletin's not the paper I fell in love with. Hasn't been for a long time. Just too damn stubborn to let it go.

speaker: KAREN
line: You really think Ellison was taking money from Fisk?

speaker: BEN
line: Don't know. Explains a lot.

speaker: KAREN
line: So, uh, what do we do next?

speaker: BEN
line: Thinking I might start a blog. Hear that's all you kids read these days.

speaker: KAREN
line: I thought you hated that kind of shit.

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah, but you can reach an awful lot of people that way if you got the right story to tell.

speaker: KAREN
line: You're gonna write about Fisk killing his father?

speaker: BEN
line: I'm going to write about all of it... tonight. Get it out there. Fisk wants to sue me... at least I know a couple decent lawyers.

speaker: KAREN
line: This is gonna change everything, Ben. It has to.

speaker: BEN
line: One foot in front of the other. I'll send you the link when it's up. We'll go from there, okay? Call you in the morning.

speaker: KAREN
line: Okay. Good night.

speaker: MATT
line: Karen? Karen? You in there?

speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah, just a minute. I'm sorry.

speaker: MATT
line: We, uh, locking this now?

speaker: KAREN
line: Seems like a good idea.

speaker: MATT
line: Yeah... It's, uh, late. You should go home.

speaker: KAREN
line: Matt? Is this what we are now? Three people who don't even talk to each other? I know this guy... We were close once. He told me if I, uh... I'd have to push the people that I care about away... if I wanted to be effective at what I do.

speaker: MATT
line: Seems like you listened.

speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah. I thought I didn't. This guy, he has a way of, uh... getting in your head, you know? And here's the thing... I had a really shitty night. The kind where you think you've seen the bottom of humanity, and the pit just keeps getting deeper, you know? I... I can't... I can't do this alone. I can't... I can't take another step.

speaker: KAREN
line: You're not alone, Matt. You never were.

speaker: BEN (TYPING)
line: I've made mistakes... in the years since I was a boy. I try to learn from them, but it isn't always enough.

speaker: BEN
line: Get out of my house.

speaker: FISK
line: I'll leave. But first, I'd... I'd like to have a conversation with you. Off the record, of course.

speaker: BEN
line: You think I believe anything you have to say?

speaker: FISK
line: Well, I... I promise that I'll be honest with you, Mr. Urich. Whether you choose to believe, that's up to you.

speaker: BEN
line: All right. Let's hear it.

speaker: FISK
line: I want to apologize. I thought that your days of being relevant were past. And for thinking that, I... I'm truly sorry.

speaker: BEN
line: Apology accepted. You know where the door is.

speaker: FISK
line: Oh... I know you lost your position at the Bulletin.

speaker: BEN
line: News travels fast.

speaker: FISK
line: After your article on... Union Allied, I took precautions. I didn't want to be surprised by any more exposés.

speaker: BEN
line: Figured you had somebody at the paper on your payroll.

speaker: FISK
line: As I said, I try to learn from my mistakes.

speaker: BEN
line: You're not the only one.

speaker: FISK
line: And do you think that rambling on the Internet will change anything?

speaker: BEN
line: People seek the truth... no matter where they find it.

speaker: FISK
line: That may have been the case when you and I were young. This world around us is preoccupied with celebrity weddings and... videos of cats. But... complicated issues, issues that matter... they take too much focus. They take too much time away from texting and the thousand channels on the satellite dish.

speaker: BEN
line: Guess I have more faith in humanity.

speaker: FISK
line: Ah. So did Christ, if I recall.

speaker: BEN
line: I'll go. Just one more thing. Were you alone when you spoke to my mother?

speaker: FISK
line: Your guy at the Bulletin.

speaker: BEN
line: Yes, I received a call that was upsetting.

speaker: FISK
line: Were you alone?

speaker: BEN
line: Yeah... I was alone.

speaker: FISK
line: Wesley, was that you?

speaker: BEN
line: Wesley?

speaker: FISK
line: Yes, I didn't think so. You're a man of principle, of conviction. I understand that, I even admire it. But you went after my mother. That's not something that I can forgive.

speaker: BEN
line: I wrote a lot of stories in my years pushing ink. You know how many times people have threatened me... get me to keep my mouth shut?

speaker: FISK

line: I told you I would keep you safe, Karen... when he came after you over Union Allied. That hasn't changed. Everyone that's taken money from him, everyone that's helped him tear this city apart... they're all gonna get what's coming to them... along with Wilson Fisk.

line: I'm not a religious man... but I've read bits and pieces over the years. Curiosity more than faith. But this one story... There was a man. The Samaritan tended to the traveler's wounds, applying oil and wine. And he carried him to an inn, gave him all the money he had for the owner to take care of the traveler, as the Samaritan, he... continued on his journey. speaker: FISK
line: I always thought that I was the Samaritan in that story. It's funny, isn't it? How even the best of men can be... deceived by their true nature.

line: What the hell does that mean?

speaker: FISK
line: It means that I'm not the Samaritan. That I'm not the priest, or the Levite. That I am the ill intent... who set upon the traveler on a road that he should not have been on.

speaker: FATHER LANTOM
line: "Precious in the eyes of the Lord... is the death of his saints." Well... Elliot Grote was no saint. He was human... deeply flawed. Every Sunday, for as far as I remember... Elliot would come here... friendless and alone... to sit. Right there in that pew. Often, I would see him take... whatever money he had... crumpled one hundreds, loose change... a Rolex watch one time... and put it in the collection plate... hoping for redemption. Which would never come. Praying for the light... but Elliot died still in the dark... with no one to mourn his loss... except the three of you. And so, we might say... one life gone... one sinful life... but one person is not just one person. In each of us, there is a world... webbing out, reaching others. Creating reactions. Sometimes equal... sometimes opposite. We rush to say, one life gone... but each of us is a world. And today, a world has been lost.

line: Why... why am I here? Why did you ask me to stay?

line: Mr. Castle...

line: After your family was...

speaker: FRANK

speaker: FRANK

line: The plates, were they... Were they on the table, or did they get into the sink?

line: Um... Uh... I think, washed. In the rack.

line: How about in the next room, did you... Did you see that piano that was there?

speaker: FRANK
line: Yeah. Yeah.

speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah?

line: My son, Frank Junior, he... He used to grab a handful of cookies and take 'em and hide 'em in that bench. You know, he'd play soldier. Guard it, protect it.

speaker: KAREN
line: Oh, yeah?

speaker: FRANK
line: Then he'd fall asleep down there. We'd find him... He'd be sleeping on a pile of... pile of cookie crumbs.

line: Yeah, I, um... When I was little girl, I did the same thing. Except ginger snaps and, um, broom closet.

speaker: FRANK
line: Oh, yeah?

speaker: KAREN
line: Pretend it was a spaceship. Take me... far away.

speaker: FRANK
line: Did you?

speaker: KAREN
line: Yeah. I guess we need that, right? We need to get away sometimes.

line: I went up into the kids' bedrooms. There were drawings on the walls and, uh, sports trophies on the dressers.

speaker: FRANK
line: Yeah, I was gone a lot, so I didn't... I missed a lot of that.

speaker: KAREN
line: There were toys... scattered all over the ground, um... A lot of plastic dinosaurs.

line: Yeah, those were my little girl's. Those were Lisa's. When she was little, she used to make these little noises when she played with them.

speaker: KAREN
line: What about the little... the little car? Like a... Like a remote-controlled Jeep.

speaker: FRANK
line: Yeah, yeah, that, uh... That was Frank Junior's. I got that for him for his seventh birthday. He used to... Yeah, he drove me crazy with that thing.

speaker: KAREN
line: Look, Frank, it's... It's really not for me to say... but they clearly loved you. Very much.

speaker: FRANK
line: Yeah... Okay... Here.

speaker: KAREN
line: Thank you.

line: Thank you, ma'am.

line: For what?

line: You helped... You helped me remember.

line: You're welcome. If you wanna ask your questions, you can go ahead.

line: It's your lucky day, Mr. Castle.

line: The six Dogs of Hell gang members you wiped out in Delaware? Won't be an issue anymore. line: And the bad?

line: She wouldn't budge on protective custody. He's gonna have to be in general pop.

speaker: KAREN
line: Uh, no, that's bullshit. All right? He'll be... He'll be surrounded by criminals, people out for his blood.

line: Sounds like a party.

line: No doubt you can handle yourself, but I think Reyes is betting on the gangs here. Legally, though? I think this is the best possible deal we're gonna make right now. So... I recommend you take it.

speaker: FRANK
line: Okay.

line: Okay, so, when the judge and Reyes come in... all you have to do is say three simple words. "Guilty, Your Honor." And you'll never have to see us again.

line: Case number 4854, The People v. Frank Castle. Do you waive the reading of the charges?

line: Counselor, please control your client.

speaker: FRANK
line: Do you hear me?

line: I'm sorry, Your Honor.

line: Holy shit.

line: If you had to sum up Frank Castle, how would you do it?

speaker: SCHOONOVER
line: I would say Frank Castle is a man who would gladly give his life to keep others safe.

speaker: FOGGY
line: And the crimes he's accused of today? Could the man you knew have committed them?

speaker: SCHOONOVER
line: Absolutely not. Lieutenant Frank Castle that I know is a hero. A man who deserves our respect... and our gratitude. Not the same man.

speaker: FOGGY
line: Thank you, sir. No more questions, Your Honor.

speaker: JUDGE
line: People?

speaker: REYES
line: I'd like to personally thank you for your service to this country, Colonel. My father served in Vietnam.

speaker: SCHOONOVER
line: Do you know what he told me about medals?

speaker: REYES
line: No, ma'am.

speaker: SCHOONOVER
line: He said the only people who truly know what happened are the ones that were there.

speaker: REYES
